title: Plan Stamping, for Software
why_read: A thoughtful essay on what it should mean to 'approve' AI-generated code, using a real security bug (a reusable password-reset token) as a sharp illustrative example.
analysis: The author describes a real failure where an AI coding agent implemented password reset but didn't invalidate the token after first use, a bug the human reviewer approved without catching. From there, the piece explores the deeper question of what a human's sign-off on AI-written code should actually guarantee, drawing an analogy to how other professions formalized what a signature or stamp means. This is a genuinely interesting angle on accountability and review processes as AI-generated code becomes more common, going beyond typical hype or fear pieces. It's more of a reflective essay than a technical how-to, but the underlying question about auditability and review rigor is a real and underexplored one.
